analysis.summary: REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS Supply and Implementation of a Fleet Tracking and Logistics Management Platform (450 Vehicles) Reference No: KMDS/IT/2026/RFQ-031 Issued by: Karachi Metropolitan Distribution Services (KMDS) Date of Issue: Friday, 12 June 2026 Procurement Method: Single Stage - Two Envelope Procedure Contact Email: procurement@kmds.com.pk

requirements.text: The successful bidder (hereinafter "the Supplier") shall be responsible for:
The Platform shall reach operational acceptance within twenty (20) weeks of purchase order, in accordance with the following indicative schedule:
A pre-bid meeting shall be held online via Microsoft Teams on Thursday, 2 July 2026 at 11:30 PKT; the joining link shall be shared with firms that register their interest by email.
Technical envelopes shall be opened the same day at 14:30 PKT.
EL-1: The bidder must be a company registered in Pakistan with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) and must hold valid NTN and STRN registrations with active taxpayer status.
EL-2: The bidder must have been in continuous operation in software development, telematics or systems integration for at least three (3) years as of the date of this RFQ.
EL-3: The bidder must hold a valid ISO 9001 quality management certification;
ISO/IEC 27001 certification is additionally required because the Platform will process commercially sensitive delivery and customer location data.
Both certifications are mandatory.

EL-4: The bidder must have successfully delivered at least two (2) vehicle tracking, telematics or logistics management projects in the last five (5) years, each covering at least 150 vehicles or with a contract value of at least PKR 25 million.
EL-5: The bidder must have an average annual turnover of at least PKR 80 million over the last three (3) audited financial years.

EL-6: The bidder must maintain a support presence in Karachi, either an existing office or a written undertaking to designate Karachi-based support staff before operational acceptance, to meet the on-site response times in Section 6.
EL-7: The bidder must submit an affidavit that it is not blacklisted by any federal, provincial or local government entity or public sector organisation in Pakistan.

EL-8: The bidder must furnish bid security equal to two percent (2%) of the quoted price, in the form of a pay order or bank guarantee from a scheduled bank in favour of Karachi Metropolitan Distribution Services.
EL-9: All proposed GPS tracking devices must be type-approved by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA).

FT-01: The Supplier shall provide GPS/IoT tracking devices supporting GPS and GLONASS positioning, 4G LTE connectivity with 2G fallback, an internal backup battery of at least 4 hours, ignition sensing, and a minimum ingress protection rating of IP65 for externally mounted components.

FT-02: Devices shall report position, speed, heading, ignition state and configured event data at intervals not exceeding 10 seconds while in motion and 5 minutes while stationary, with store-and-forward buffering of at least 5,000 records during connectivity loss.

FT-03: Fuel level sensors shall achieve an accuracy of plus or minus 3 percent after per-vehicle calibration, and the Platform shall detect and alert refuelling and fuel drain events with timestamp, location and estimated volume.
FT-04: Temperature sensors in refrigerated units shall report at intervals not exceeding 60 seconds, with configurable thresholds and breach alerts to dispatchers and in the driver application.
FT-05: The Supplier shall manage SIM provisioning and airtime for all devices for the full two-year support period, with monthly connectivity reporting.

FT-06: The Platform shall provide live map tracking of all 450 vehicles with at most 15 seconds of latency, historical trip playback for a minimum of 12 months online, and geofencing with entry, exit and dwell-time alerts.

FT-07: The Platform shall provide route planning and optimisation that produces multi-stop delivery routes for at least 300 daily orders across the three distribution centres, accounting for vehicle capacity, delivery time windows and zone restrictions, and shall recalculate routes when orders change.

FT-08: The Platform shall compute a driver behaviour score per driver per period, based at a minimum on harsh braking, harsh acceleration, over-speeding against configurable road-class limits, sharp cornering, excessive idling and unauthorised stops, and shall produce ranked driver league reports.

FT-09: The Platform shall integrate with the KMDS warehouse management system through documented REST APIs to receive dispatch orders and return delivery status and electronic proof-of-delivery records, including recipient name, signature image, photo and geo-stamp.

FT-10: The Platform shall provide role-based dashboards for dispatchers, fleet supervisors and management, including fleet utilisation, on-time delivery percentage, kilometres run, fuel consumption versus benchmark, maintenance due lists and exception summaries, with scheduled email reports and export to Excel and CSV.
FT-11: The Platform shall maintain a vehicle maintenance module covering service schedules by kilometres and calendar, defect reporting from the driver application, and workshop job records.

FT-12: The driver mobile application shall operate on Android 10 or later, shall support Urdu and English interfaces, and shall function in offline mode with automatic synchronisation upon reconnection.

FT-13: The Platform shall be hosted in a data centre or cloud region located in Pakistan, shall enforce role-based access control with multi-factor authentication for administrative users, shall encrypt data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher, and shall provide a complete audit trail of user actions.

FT-14: The Platform shall provide open, documented APIs sufficient for KMDS to extract its own data, and all tracking and operational data shall remain the property of KMDS and shall be handed over in a standard machine-readable format upon contract end.

FT-15: The Supplier shall migrate vehicle master data, driver records and approximately 6,500 customer delivery locations from existing spreadsheets and registers, with validation and sign-off by KMDS operations.

FT-16: The Supplier shall deliver role-based training for up to 12 dispatchers, 10 fleet supervisors, 8 workshop staff and 6 managers, together with bilingual quick reference guides and administrator documentation.

The Supplier shall provide comprehensive support and maintenance for twenty-four (24) months from operational acceptance, including all software updates, device warranty with advance replacement from the spares pool, sensor recalibration, airtime management and helpdesk support from 08:00 to 20:00 PKT, seven days a week.
The Platform shall achieve a monthly availability of at least 99.5 percent, excluding scheduled maintenance notified at least three (3) working days in advance.

Critical faults (Platform unavailable or live tracking down fleet-wide) shall be responded to within 30 minutes and resolved within 6 hours; faulty in-vehicle devices shall be replaced within 2 working days in Karachi.
The Supplier shall provide a quarterly service review report covering availability, fault statistics, device health and connectivity performance.
Quotations shall be evaluated under a two-envelope quality and cost based method.
Technical proposals shall be scored against the criteria below; financial envelopes of bidders scoring at least 60 of the 80 technical points shall be opened and scored.
The contract shall be awarded to the bidder with the highest combined score:

The lowest evaluated financial quotation shall receive the full 20 financial points; other quotations shall be scored as 20 multiplied by the ratio of the lowest quoted price to the price under evaluation.
Quotations exceeding the approved budget shall be rejected.

Prices shall be quoted in Pakistani Rupees inclusive of all applicable taxes and duties, broken down into: hardware and installation; software licences or subscription; integration and data migration; training; and year-wise support and connectivity charges.
Payment shall be made as follows: 20 percent on completion of milestone M2;
No advance payment shall be made.
Bidders shall answer the following questions in the technical envelope.
Each answer shall not exceed two (2) pages and shall be specific to KMDS operations:

The technical envelope shall contain the eligibility evidence for criteria EL-1 to EL-9, the technical compliance statement against requirements FT-01 to FT-16, the questionnaire responses, the implementation plan and CVs of key staff, and one USB drive with the complete technical quotation in searchable PDF format.
The financial envelope shall contain the priced quotation form and the bid security instrument.
No financial figures shall appear in the technical envelope.

If the Supplier fails to achieve operational acceptance (milestone M5) within twenty (20) weeks of purchase order for reasons attributable to the Supplier, KMDS shall deduct liquidated damages at the rate of 0.25 percent (zero point two five percent) of the total contract price per week of delay or part thereof, up to a maximum of eight percent (8%) of the total contract price, after which KMDS may cancel the purchase order, encash the bid security or performance security then held, and procure the platform from another supplier at the Supplier's risk and cost.

During the support period, service credits of 2 percent of the quarterly support fee shall apply for each 0.1 percentage point shortfall below the 99.5 percent monthly availability target, capped at 20 percent of the quarterly support fee.

The successful bidder shall furnish a performance security of five percent (5%) of the contract value within ten (10) days of the purchase order, valid for the full contract term plus sixty (60) days.
All communications shall quote reference KMDS/IT/2026/RFQ-031.

questions.text: Device Specification and Certification: Specify the make and model of the proposed tracking devices, fuel sensors and temperature sensors, their PTA type approval status, mounting and tamper protection approach, and your device failure rate experience from comparable deployments.

Platform Architecture: Describe the Platform architecture, including the hosting arrangement in Pakistan, multi-tenancy model if any, data ingestion capacity, latency safeguards for live tracking of 450 vehicles, backup and disaster recovery arrangements, and the security controls applied at each layer.

Route Optimisation Approach: Explain how your route optimisation engine builds and re-optimises multi-stop routes under vehicle capacity, time window and zone constraints, the typical computation time for a 300-order daily plan, and how dispatchers can manually adjust optimised routes.

WMS Integration: Describe your proposed approach to integrating with the KMDS warehouse management system, including the API patterns, message formats, error handling and reconciliation arrangements, and a summary of two comparable integrations you have delivered.

Driver Scoring Methodology: Describe the events, weightings and normalisation method used in your driver behaviour scoring, how scores remain fair across different routes and vehicle types, and how the scoring has measurably reduced incidents or fuel consumption in past deployments.

Support and Spares Model: Describe your support organisation for this contract, including Karachi-based resources, escalation tiers, the spares pool and advance replacement process, sensor recalibration schedule, and the reporting you will provide against the service levels in Section 6.

draft.title: Relevant Experience & Past Performance
draft.content:
**Integrated WMS & Transport Management for 3PL Provider** [CAP-048] — Third-Party Logistics (3PL) Company (Private Enterprise), 2025, USD 530k, 16 months.
Second-generation deployment combining our WMS with a transport management module for a 3PL operating nine warehouses and contracted line-haul fleets: multi-client inventory segregation with client billing engines, load planning and carrier assignment, and milestone-based shipment tracking exposed through a customer portal and APIs. Route optimization reduced empty backhaul through load consolidation suggestions. Delivered with phased go-lives to avoid client disruption and training for 420 operations staff. _Outcome: Billing leakage recovered 7% of revenue via automated client invoicing; truck utilization up 21%; new 3PL client onboarding time cut from 8 weeks to 12 days._

**Ambulance Fleet Tracking & Dispatch for Emergency Service** [CAP-047] — Provincial Emergency Rescue Service (Government), 2023, USD 490k, 14 months.
Built on our courier telematics platform to deliver computer-aided dispatch and GPS tracking for 1,400 ambulances: nearest-unit recommendation with live traffic ETAs, call-taker console integrated with the 1122 control rooms, and hospital-arrival notifications to emergency departments. Vehicle health telemetry schedules preventive maintenance to keep fleet readiness high. Included control-room operator training across 36 districts and 24/7 platform support under SLA. _Outcome: Average emergency response time improved 2.6 minutes province-wide; fleet out-of-service rate halved through telemetry-driven maintenance; 1.8 million emergencies dispatched on the platform._

**Route Optimization Engine for LPG Distribution** [CAP-029] — LPG Marketing & Distribution Company (Private Enterprise), 2022, USD 380k, 12 months.
Built a vehicle routing and scheduling engine for daily LPG cylinder distribution to 11,000 retail points, solving capacity- and time-window-constrained VRP with traffic-aware travel times and driver shift rules. Dispatchers get suggested route plans with manual override, and an Android driver app handles proof-of-delivery, cylinder reconciliation and cash collection. The optimizer integrates with the company's SAP order pipeline through nightly and intraday syncs. _Outcome: Fleet kilometers reduced 17% for the same delivery volume; deliveries per vehicle per day up 22%; cash reconciliation discrepancies down 88% via digital POD._

**Warehouse Management System for FMCG Distributor** [CAP-028] — FMCG Distribution Group (Private Enterprise), 2020, USD 470k, 15 months.
Implemented a warehouse management system across five distribution centers with barcode-driven receiving, putaway, wave picking, batch/expiry (FEFO) control and cycle counting on Android handheld terminals. Integrated with the distributor's ERP for orders and inventory sync, and added a yard/dock scheduling module to smooth inbound congestion. Provided floor-level training and capacity building for 350 warehouse staff with bilingual Urdu/English work instructions. _Outcome: Picking accuracy rose to 99.7%; order-to-dispatch lead time cut 46%; inventory shrinkage reduced 63% in the first year._

**GPS Fleet Tracking & Telematics Platform for National Courier** [CAP-027] — National Courier & Express Company (Private Enterprise), 2019, USD 560k, 18 months.
Deployed a GPS fleet tracking and telematics platform for 8,000 vehicles and riders, ingesting live location, ignition, speed and harsh-driving events with geofencing around hubs and delivery zones. Control-tower dashboards give route replay, ETA prediction and SLA breach alerts to regional operations teams, while driver-behavior scoring feeds safety coaching. Integrated with the courier's shipment system so customer service sees parcel-level vehicle locations in real time. _Outcome: On-time delivery improved 14 percentage points; fuel cost per route down 11% through idling and route-deviation control; vehicle utilization up 19%._

**Port Container Tracking & Customs e-Clearance Integration** [CAP-030] — Private Container Terminal Operator (Private Enterprise), 2016, USD 410k, 16 months.
Developed a container tracking and gate-automation system for a port terminal, integrating OCR gate cameras, RFID truck tags and yard position updates with the terminal operating system. Built two-way EDI/API integration with the national customs clearance system (WeBOC) for examination holds and release messages, plus a shipper portal for real-time container status and e-DO workflows. Reduced manual paperwork at gates through digital job orders. _Outcome: Average truck gate turnaround cut from 41 to 13 minutes; customs release-to-gate-out time reduced 35%; portal adoption by 1,900 freight forwarders._
